title: Bones of the skull (right lateral, color-coded)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Location
Forehead and the roofs of the orbits.
Articulates with
Parietal bones at the coronal suture, and the sphenoid, ethmoid, nasal, lacrimal and zygomatic bones and the maxillae.
Features
Supraorbital margin with its notch or foramen; the frontal sinuses lie within it.
Location
Side and roof of the cranial vault, one on each side.
Articulates with

Frontal bone at the coronal suture, the opposite parietal bone at the sagittal suture, the occipital bone at the lambdoid suture, the temporal bone at the squamous suture, and the greater wing of the sphenoid.
Location
Side and base of the skull, around the ear.
Articulates with
Parietal, occipital, sphenoid and zygomatic bones, and the mandible at the temporomandibular joint.
Features
Squamous, petrous, mastoid and tympanic parts and the styloid process. The petrous part houses the middle and inner ear.
hy: At the pterion the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet and the skull is thin. A fracture here can tear the middle meningeal artery and cause an epidural hematoma.

Its openings and what passes through: internal acoustic meatus (CN VII and VIII), stylomastoid foramen (CN VII leaves the skull), and, between it and the occipital bone, the jugular foramen (CN IX, X, XI and the internal jugular vein).

rows: Location
Back and base of the skull.
Articulates with
Parietal bones at the lambdoid suture, the temporal bones, the sphenoid, and the atlas (C1) at the occipital condyles.
Features
Foramen magnum, occipital condyles, hypoglossal canals and the external occipital protuberance.
hy: The foramen magnum transmits the lower end of the brainstem, the vertebral arteries and the spinal roots of the accessory nerve. The hypoglossal canal transmits CN XII.

rows: Location
Center of the skull base, behind the orbits. It is shaped like a butterfly.
Articulates with
Frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital and ethmoid bones, and the zygomatic and palatine bones and the vomer.
Features
Body with the sella turcica, which holds the pituitary gland, and the sphenoidal sinuses; greater and lesser wings; pterygoid processes.
hy: Its openings and what passes through: optic canal (CN II, ophthalmic artery), superior orbital fissure (CN III, IV, V1, VI), foramen rotundum (V2), foramen ovale (V3), foramen spinosum (middle meningeal artery).

rows: Location
Cheekbone. It also forms part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, greater wing of the sphenoid, maxilla, and the zygomatic process of the temporal bone, with which it forms the zygomatic arch.
Location
Upper jaw. It forms most of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit and the side wall of the nasal cavity.
Articulates with
Frontal, nasal, lacrimal, ethmoid, zygomatic and palatine bones, the vomer, the inferior nasal concha and the opposite maxilla.
Features
Maxillary sinus, infraorbital foramen, and the alveolar process that carries the upper teeth.
Location
Lower jaw. It is the only freely movable bone of the skull.
Articulates with
Temporal bones, at the two temporomandibular joints.
Features
Body, angle and ramus; coronoid and condylar processes; the mandibular foramen, where the inferior alveolar nerve enters, and the mental foramen.
Location
Bridge of the nose, one on each side of the midline.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid, the maxilla and the opposite nasal bone.
Location
Front of the medial wall of the orbit. It is the smallest bone of the face.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, ethmoid, maxilla and inferior nasal concha.
Features
With the maxilla it forms the fossa for the lacrimal sac and the start of the nasolacrimal canal.
